title: memory-halo-evictor-with-priority-dampening
author: Marcus Li
description: Adds a two-part approach to reduce KV cache fragmentation and noisy spill activity under bursty workloads. Part A introduces a lightweight 'memory halo' allocation layer that reserves small adjacent slots around hot KV entries to reduce micro-fragmentation when small values are written/updated; the halo is opportunistically reclaimed under pressure. Part B implements a priority-dampening eviction controller: eviction candidates have a dampening score computed from age, access frequency, tenant priority, and continuous-batching latency sensitivity. The controller biases spill I/O to low-priority tenants and uses an exponential backoff before evicting recently-accessed halo-adjacent slots to avoid thrashing. This PR ties the controller into the existing scheduler so evictions are scheduled on background lanes that avoid interfering with token-generation work by respecting kernel scheduling windows. Motivation: in production experiments we observed repeated micro-spills during short update bursts which amplified tail latency and increased storage IOPS by ~35% on generated traces. The new approach reduces small-block spill counts and improves p50/p95 token latency behind busiest models. Implementation notes: - feature flag: kv.memory_halo.enabled (default: off) - config knobs: halo_size_bytes (default 256), halo_reclaim_threshold_percent (default 12), dampening_decay_half_life_ms (default 1500), tenant_spill_priority_map - scheduler hook: eviction_hint API extended with scheduling_tier and preferred_kernel_affinity - monitoring: new metrics kv.halo_reclaimed_bytes, kv.eviction_dampening_score, kv.tenant_spill_count The description below lists what changed, tests run, and rollout plan. Changes: - New module: runtime/kv/halo_allocator.{h,cc} implementing compact halo ranges and opportunistic reclaim - Eviction controller moved to runtime/kv/evictor_controller.cc with dampening logic and tenant-priority spill routing - Scheduler integration in runtime/scheduler/eviction_scheduler.cc - Config + feature flags in infra/config/kv_config.yaml - Metrics and dashboard graphs added under observability/dashboards/kv_halo.json Tests and validation: - Unit tests for halo allocator and dampening math (runtime/kv/*_test.cc) - Integration test: simulated bursty update workload with mixed tenant priorities; verifies spill counts and latency - Loadbench: 48-hour soak on canary cluster with continuous batching enabled and workloads approximating multi-tenant PLG traffic Results (canary): - spill IOPS down 28% on average across samples - median token latency improved 6% and p95 improved 12% for affected models - memory overhead observed ~0.8% at default halo size - no observed increase in GC or scheduler contention Rollout plan: 1) enable feature flag in staging for 48h with monitoring alarms, 2) opt-in on select canary nodes with low-priority tenants for 72h, 3) progressive ramp to 25% of capacity, 4) full rollout after stable signal. Backwards compatibility: toggled by feature flag; safe default off. Related work: builds on prior eviction prioritization RFC (ENG-3480) and interacts with batching improvements in ENG-4410.

review_comments: Asha Patel (2026-02-20): Great approach. Two asks: please quantify worst-case reclaim latency and add a safety cap to halo_reclaim to avoid starving other allocators.
Marcus Li (2026-02-21): Added safety cap (halo_reclaim_threshold_percent) and documented reclaim latency in allocator comments; added test for reclaim timing.
Diego Ramos (2026-02-24): Controller logic looks sound but please simplify dampening score math to avoid FP instability in long-running counters.
Marcus Li (2026-02-25): Switched to fixed-point dampening accumulator; added regression test; CI rerun required due to flakiness.
Linnea Jorgensen (2026-03-01): Verified integration on canary cluster and reviewed dashboards; minor style nits addressed.
Asha Patel (2026-03-02): Approved after runtime tests passed and canary signal was stable for 72h.
ci_summary: Initial CI run failed on one flaky allocator timing test; fixed by using a deterministic clock in tests and re-run succeeded.
performance_notes: Canary benchmarks show 28% reduction in small-block spill counts and 12% p95 latency improvement for heavy-update traces. Memory overhead <1% at default halo size. Dampening reduces eviction churn on hot keys during batching bursts.
rollback_instructions: Flip kv.memory_halo.enabled=false via runtime-config and drain canary nodes; eviction controller will revert to previous policy automatically. If eviction controller is causing regressions, set kv.eviction_dampening.mode=off and restart runtime agents.
release_notes:
- Introduced Memory Halo allocator to reduce KV cache fragmentation and micro-spill activity.
- Added eviction dampening controller to prioritize tenant-spill and reduce eviction thrash.
- Config flags: kv.memory_halo.enabled, kv.eviction_dampening.*
- Metrics: kv.halo_reclaimed_bytes, kv.eviction_dampening_score, kv.tenant_spill_count
merge_commit: 6b4f90c: squash merge - memory halo evictor with priority dampening
notes_for_ops: Watch kv.halo_reclaimed_bytes and kv.tenant_spill_count for unexpected spikes. Add temporary alert if kv.eviction_dampening_score > 0.9 for sustained 10m intervals. Be prepared to toggle halo feature flag if storage IOPS regress.
testing_instructions: Run runtime/kv/halo_allocator_test and runtime/kv/evictor_controller_test locally. Use loadbench scenario 'kv-burst-updates.json' with tenant profiles to reproduce canary results. Use feature flags via config to enable on individual nodes.
notes: This design intentionally biases towards reduced I/O churn at small memory cost. Ops and DB teams should monitor storage tail latency during the ramp.
